arms.better: tm found the relevant progress implementation and produced a passing fix against the merged hidden tests, but its recorded 471,917 tokens and 647-second run are high for this narrow defect; the log shows multiple exploratory test passes and creating then deleting a temporary test file. The CLI's staged flow is understandable, and the final `tm run` message correctly tells the user to review and accept the submitted work, though a one-shot user may expect `tm run` itself to finish the ticket rather than stop at a review handoff. Better guided narrowing after the first relevant hit, targeted verification before broad test runs, and a more compact user-visible run summary with elapsed time and token usage would reduce effort and make the handoff more obvious.

OpenCode quickly located the flush guard, stated a scoped implementation and test plan, and reported the failure when its first browser test exposed that Fetch may provide a null response body. It then extended the fix to cover that path and reran the focused progress tests successfully. It could improve by recognizing the null-body response path before its first test attempt and preserving the focused verification result clearly alongside the unrelated full-suite XO/WebKit failures found during independent verification.
